item.title: Buccaneers at Bears: Initial injury report for Week 9
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Kenny Gainwell #1 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers began preparations for their Week 9 matchup against the Chicago Bears on Wednesday, releasing their first injury report ahead of Sunday night’s game at Soldier Field. Tampa Bay listed eight players on the initial report, including three who did not participate in practice. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) remained sidelined after missing the team’s previous two games, leaving his availability for Sunday uncertain. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) also did not practice and is expected to miss the matchup after suffering an MCL sprain in the Buccaneers’ Week 8 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Defensive lineman Elijah Roberts was the third player held out of practice, although his absence was listed as personal rather than injury-related. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited participants Wednesday. Meanwhile, quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), guard Cody Mauch (back) and tight end Cade Otton (thumb) participated fully. The Buccaneers are coming off a 16-0 shutout victory over Atlanta, their second consecutive win, and will look to continue that momentum against a Chicago team that enters the matchup at 6-2 following a Monday night victory over Seattle. Tampa Bay will have two more practice sessions before the team’s final injury report is released Friday, providing a clearer picture of who will be available for Sunday’s contest. The Buccaneers and Bears are scheduled to kick off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.

The Colts needed a quarterback who could elevate the entire roster, and I mean elevate it to a level most teams have reached in the last five years … the postseason. But has Daniel Jones ever been that kind QB? No. We just saw that in New York. So why did the Colts pay him just to ask him to elevate a bad WR room, while he’s coming off an achilles injury. It just doesn’t make sense. Not to mention the defense has been one of the worst in the league, if they were even league average the Daniel Jones discourse wouldn’t be as loud, because the Colts would likely have more than just 2 wins. Week after week we see defenses sell out to stop the run while Daniel Jones tries to pass his way behind the sticks in environments that aren’t optimized for a QB like him to be successful. So yes, Daniel Jones has not played good football. But if you’re going to hate him for the way he’s played, hate the front office first. Because I think Daniel Jones can play a lot better than he has, and maybe if he’s traded he’ll get a chance to show that again.

item.description: Ravens Trading for Ex-Patriots QB Could Impact New England's Playoff Chances originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the unfortunate news that the Baltimore Ravens continue to get surrounding their quarterback room, with Lamar Jackson expected to be out for possibly the remainder of the season and backup quarterback Snoop Huntley now out for the year, it was fair to wonder if Baltimore could be interested in a guy like Mac Jones, the former New England Patriots starting quarterback who is now with the San Francisco 49ers. While it remained uncertain whether the 49ers would actually move on from him, it felt like if a team was going to be desperate, it would be Baltimore. However, that's not the case, as reports have now indicated that the Ravens are trading for Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett has been playing decent football throughout the season but was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew. While this trade doesn't directly impact New England, there are some reasons why it could. "The Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a trade to send quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend. The Ravens lost starting quarterback Lamar Jackson to a potentially season-ending thumb injury that will require surgery. Backup Tyler "Snoop" Huntley has a turf toe injury that will end his season, sources told Schefter and Rapoport earlier Wednesday," ESPN reported . The Ravens are undoubtedly one of the better teams in the NFL when everything is right. Which is why their victory party wasn't just about sports. It was a celebration of who we are. All of us. And particularly a celebration of women. This was our first sports party for a professional women's team, representing the half of society shut out of sports for too long. One that used love and friendship and the fight for equity as keys to victory. This is the first women's professional team to stand on the mountaintop with the Bay Area's other sports icons. The Valkyries started their day in Oakland, the city where they work and practice; where their star player, Gabby Williams , spent much of her youth and where she relocated when Golden State signed her last spring. "Oakland's just a culture, a familial feeling," Williams said this week. After an Oakland ceremony, the team journeyed across the water to San Francisco. Along the way Williams and Natalie Nakase sat in the cockpit and drove the boat, under the watchful eye of the crew. If you were looking for a metaphor, that was a perfect one: the brilliant little coach and the graceful star piloting the team to where it needed to go. When I first met Nakase in March 2025, she told me she had a team full of "killers." And she told me she expected to win, yes, even with an expansion team. "Yeah, everyone thinks we're gonna lose," she said during our hour-long talk. "Go ahead and doubt us." I left smiling at her bravado. A brand new coach of a brand new team with championship aspirations. Cute. She envisioned it. She believed it. She drove the boat, straight to a title. As the amateur captains pointed toward the Ferry Building, Alcatraz - the prison island that led Tiffany Hayes to nickname the team's lock ‘em up defense "Valkatraz" - loomed on the starboard side. Standing down on the prow of the boat was Kiah Stokes , the warden of Valkatraz. She was wearing a shirt with a replica of ESPN's July 28 "Basketball Power Index," listing the five teams the outlet's analytics projected as having the best chance to win the WNBA title: the Fever, the Aces, the Lynx, the Liberty and the Dream. Yeah, the Valkyries were relishing their moment of triumph. As they pulled into the Port of San Francisco (Williams and Nakase had abandoned the helm and let the pros dock the boat), they were greeted by an incredible sight: thousands of lavender-clad fans screaming and cheering their arrival, five lavender double-decker buses with their larger-than-life images on the side. Family members were told, "go to the bus with her face on it." Fans lined the route, from the Ferry Building to Oracle Park, 10 deep. Hundreds more stood on roofs and lined balconies to watch. Dykes on Bikes kicked off the procession, and Nakase - having the time of her life, with her family on her bus - ended it. The crowd was as joyous and diverse as the one that has packed Ballhalla ever since the Valkyries opened their doors. And the signs were epic. "We Skipped School with Violet Fever." "You are Very Good, Tiffany Hayes" (in a child's writing, in crayon). "Williams, Nakase ‘26" "4 the GAYS" "PAY EQUITY - show me the money!" "Thank you for bringing us so much joy." "Trans People Belong in Sports." "Thank you for being our safe space." The irony was not lost on anyone that the parade ended in front of Oracle Park, site of the Giant's Pride Night debacle, one of the most shameful days a local sports team has had in many years. The happy crowd chanted "Thank you, thank you" and "we love you, we love you." They smoked pot and smuggled wine glasses out from restaurants and guzzled water because their beloved coach had taught everyone the importance of staying hydrated. The fans came dressed as hot dogs ( Kaitlyn Chen 's lasting legacy) and wore purple wigs. They cheered Nancy Pelosi and Oakland mayor Barbara Lee and chanted "blue wave, blue wave." They roared for Oakland music star Kehlani, riding in Lee's convertible and shouted out Too Short's "favorite word." They waved rainbow flags and trans flags. They caught the beers that Chen and Veronica Burton tossed down to them and relished the J bubbly that Juste Jocyte sprayed on them. They parted ways to let Laeticia Amihere get to a porta potty. The crowd's response to Williams made her superstar status apparent: the woman with the Rolling Stones logo tattooed on her triceps was received like a bonafide rock star. As adoring as the crowd was, the players were just as enthusiastic in returning their love. They hopped off the buses to sign autographs and high-five. "Your baby is really cute," Burton called down to a fan. Aminata Gueye, who's had maybe the best month of her life, signed to her first WNBA contract in September and a champion by Halloween, seemed to only want to walk beside the bus, constantly hopping off to interact with the fans. The champions danced and laughed and celebrated what they had done. They had won a championship. And they won the Bay Area's collective heart. The San Antonio Spurs brought plenty of personality to the Frost Bank Center on Wednesday night, Nov. 4, ahead of their showdown with the Dallas Mavericks. From designer sneakers to statement graphic tees, the Silver and Black made sure their pregame fashion was anything but ordinary. Here's a closer look at what five Spurs players wore before tipoff. Forget wearing flashy clothes, Keldon Johnson's mustache might have been the biggest fashion statement of the night. The reigning Sixth Man of the Year arrived sporting a playful mustache that looked straight out of a 1970s detective show, giving his pregame appearance a little extra character. Johnson wore a white VALE FOREVER "Air Donald" graphic tee featuring Ronald McDonald soaring toward a basketball hoop, layered beneath a light-gray zip-up hoodie. He paired the outfit with blue jeans, Bottega Veneta Orbit low-top sneakers, and his signature "KJ" chain. Now, Stephon Castle kicked things off in a Boredom Kills Trust camouflage long-sleeve sweatshirt featuring a large graphic across the chest. The Spurs guard paired the sweatshirt with light-wash blue jeans and a cross necklace, keeping his look casual while letting the camouflage do the talking. It looks like Castle's "Area 51" teammate, Victor Wembanyama, also got the camouflage memo. At 7-foot-4, blending into a crowd isn't exactly Wembanyama's specialty, but the Spurs superstar gave it a shot Wednesday night, wearing a black zip-up hoodie layered beneath a Nike Tech Dri-FIT Woven Camo Windrunner Oversized Jacket in Neutral Olive and Black. He completed the look with gray Nike joggers and olive-green Nike sneakers, keeping things comfortable with an outdoors-inspired ensemble. With his hood up and hands tucked into his pockets, Wembanyama looked ready for a covert mission rather than an NBA matchup. Spurs guard Dylan Harper kept things coordinated in a forest-green Nike hoodie and matching sweatpants layered over a black T-shirt. He completed the outfit with black Nike sneakers and his signature diamond-encrusted No. 2 chain, adding some sparkle to his otherwise understated look. Between laid-back camouflage fits and colorful sweats, Johnson personality stands out the most as the Spurs get ready to face their in-state rival, the Dallas Mavericks. Tipoff is scheduled for 8:30 p.m. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Cheboygan volleyball to face Kingsley in D2 district title match
item.description: GRAYLING — Cheboygan volleyball is back in the district final. Playing in an MHSAA Division 2 district semifinal clash on Wednesday, Nov. 4, the Chiefs kept their season alive by capturing a 3-0 victory at Grayling (25-23, 25-23, 25-23). CHEBOYGAN JV VOLLEYBALL FINISHES 41-0: Cheboygan JV volleyball team caps off perfect 41-0 season on court TUESDAY DISTRICT ROUNDUP: Mackinaw City, NMCA advance to MHSAA district volleyball finals DISTRICT VOLLEYBALL PREVIEW: Previewing, predicting Cheboygan-area volleyball district tournaments The Chiefs took a 21-16 lead in the first set after junior Sophia Naden delivered a kill. However, Grayling, which trailed 24-16, rattled off an 8-0 run to tie the set and put all the pressure on the Chiefs. But following a Grayling attacking error, Naden hammered home another kill to give Cheboygan a one-set lead. The Vikings responded impressively by building a 16-12 lead in the second, but the Chiefs countered with a 7-3 spurt that was capped off by a kill from junior Diem Schley, which tied things up at 19. The teams went back and forth during several points, but the Chiefs took the lead for good when another kill from Naden gave Cheboygan a one-point advantage, which was then followed by another point that gave the Chiefs the set and victory. Much like the second set, the Chiefs trailed for much of the third. However, a pivotal run helped them tie the set. Polishing off the Cheboygan win was Schley, whose match-winning kill was too much for Grayling to handle. With the victory, the Chiefs (18-14-4) travel to face Kingsley (47-5-1) in a 6 p.m. district final on Thursday, Nov. 5. The Stags, who won last year's Division 3 state title, swept the Chiefs in Cheboygan earlier this season. Cheboygan fell to Ogemaw Heights in a D2 district final last year. item.description: The Cincinnati Reds’ new pitching coach goes from one of the best pitching-developmental organizations of the past few decades to one of the worst-performing pitching staffs of the 2026 season. Torres, 44, was hired by the Reds this week to replace Derek Johnson after spending the past five seasons as an assistant to highly regarded Carl Willis in Cleveland, where he worked under Reds manager Terry Francona for two of those seasons and where the Guardians’ pitching staff ranked among the top 10 in the majors all five years. “This being my first year in this lead position and having a manager with the experience that Tito has, that’s so comforting for me,” said Torres, who has less than four weeks to get to know a group of pitchers he has only seen from across the field before MLB owners impose an industry shutdown Dec. 1 with a widely anticipated labor lockout. “I’ve got a small time window here with getting to know guys,” Torres said on the day his hiring was announced, Nov. 4. “It’s getting to know them as a person first. The only thing he seems to know for sure about what he wants to bring to his new organization from Cleveland is continuity of process and even the teaching language from the minors to the majors. “I don’t know fully the values and everything they’re working through here in Cincinnati so far,” said Torres, who spent five seasons as a minor-league pitching coach and coordinator for the Guardians before joining their big-league staff. “My objective is to come in first and just listen and learn. Rhett Lowder, a No. 7 overall draft pick in 2023, showed glimpses of his spectacular six-start debut in 2024 (1.17 ERA) but struggled through injuries and inconsistency around those glimpses. And Brandon Williamson was optimistic by the end of the season that he might have put much of his injury history behind him as he looks ahead to 2027 and paying off the promise he showed as a rookie in 2023. “I don’t know any of these guys personally, but I’ve definitely seen them,” said Torres, who watched many of them regularly during spring training in Arizona and in six Ohio Cup games annually. “You look from afar and sit there and say, man, there’s a lot of talent over there,” he said. “There’s a lot of really good arm talent.” This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: How much Cleveland magic can pitching coach Joe Torres bring to Reds?

item.title: Former Flames GM Brad Treliving Suddenly Lands New Job
item.description: Maple Leafs could sign true wild card. Getty Maple Leafs linked to veteran center. Getty The Calgary Flames and general manager Brad Treliving decided to mutually part ways with one another in 2023 upon the expiration of his contract; he’d served in the role since April 2014. It wouldn’t be long before Treliving resurfaced as the general manager of the Toronto Maple Leafs, a role that he held for nearly three full seasons before being terminated in late March of last season. Now, the former Flames executive is back with a new role on the international stage. According to NHL Insider Darren Dreger, Treliving will be among many notable figures serving on Hockey Canada’s new National Teams Advisory Group. Former Calgary Flames General Manager Brad Treliving Officially Lands New Role With Hockey Canada Getty Maple Leafs linked to veteran center. As initially reported by NHL Insider Darren Dreger, Treliving will be part of multiple notable figures who will be serving in an advisory capacity. Dreger reported: “Hockey Canada will name an advisory group to assist Scott Salmond, VP of Hockey ops. Doug Armstrong, Shane Doan and Steve Yzerman will work with Salmond on World Cup,World Championship and the Olympics, identifying next management group, process,and overall planning. Brad Treliving is also working with Canada’s National Junior team, while a separate captains club has been created with Shane Doan to mentor Canadian Captains at all levels and programs. 3 former Olympic GM’s now part of Hockey Canada’s larger group.” The Flames Parted Ways With Treliving In 2023 After the Flames missed the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the second time in three years, the organization and Treliving mutually agreed to part ways. President of Hockey Operations Don Maloney explained at the time that it was time for a change after the club fell short of its goals. “We have a team that I believe should’ve been in the playoffs … not only make the playoffs, but be a hard out in the playoffs,” Maloney said via NHL.com . “We didn’t, and we failed to achieve. That starts at the management level, which I was a part of, the coaching, the players, the training, the organization. We have to do a deep look in how we operate, how we make decisions, and fix it.” “I am reviewing everything in the organization…management, coaching, players, scouting, how we first of all with what happened and why we underachieved and how we make this the best organization to obtain our goals,” he said. Unfortunately for the Flames, they’ve yet to return to the playoffs; they haven’t played beyond the regular season since 2022. The Los Angeles Dodgers should pursue CJ Abrams with a package that addresses the Washington Nationals’ pitching needs while strengthening their own infield. Emmet Sheehan, Christian Zazueta and Alex Freeland would give Washington immediate options and future upside for a hitter entering his prime. The Athletic’s Jim Bowden underscored why pursuing Abrams or Cincinnati Reds star Elly De La Cruz would make sense for the Dodgers while noting the organization’s confidence in its emerging prospects. “Taking a big swing to try to trade for the Nationals’ Abrams or the Reds’ De La Cruz also would make a lot of sense for them. That said, they feel several of their top prospects, such as outfielders Josue De Paula, Mike Sirota and Eduardo Quintero, are getting closer to being major-league ready.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This package is an editorial proposal, not a reported offer or the Nationals’ established asking price. Hypothetical trade Dodgers receive CJ Abrams Nationals receive Emmet Sheehan, Christian Zazueta and Alex Freeland Why CJ Abrams fits the Dodgers’ infield Abrams would bring a different dimension to an already formidable Dodgers lineup. He finished 2026 batting .261 with 33 home runs, 106 RBIs, 34 stolen bases and an .833 OPS. At 26, he offers power and speed across two remaining seasons of team control. The clearest fit is second base. The Nationals began preparing Abrams for that position in August, making it a more credible plan than automatically displacing Mookie Betts at shortstop. That transition still requires evaluation. item.description: New participant enters Dylan Larkin trade saga with potential three-team deal! The Dylan Larkin saga continues to dominate NHL trade chatter, and a surprising new participant has reportedly entered the picture. While the Minnesota Wild has been aggressively pursuing the Detroit Red Wings' star center for months now, it turns out the key to unlocking a deal might actually reside in Philadelphia. According to Anthony Di Marco of Daily Faceoff, Flyers general manager Daniel Brière has reportedly accepted that Larkin will not be coming to Philadelphia, as the center does not have the Flyers on his 10-team trade list. But rather than walk away from the situation entirely, Brière is apparently willing to play the role of facilitator in a potential three-team trade. https://x.com/NHLRumourReport/status/2117255407622394330?s=20 The Flyers would reportedly agree to absorb the contract of Wild forward Yakov Trenin, valued at $3.5 million, provided the return makes sense for Philadelphia. That willingness to act as a broker in the deal could be exactly what Minnesota and Detroit need to finally reach an agreement. The appeal of a three-team structure is that every organization involved can get closer to what it actually wants. Minnesota would land the top-line center it has been chasing in Larkin, while Detroit could maximize its return by pulling assets from two separate teams rather than just one. For the Flyers, the motivation reportedly goes beyond simply taking on salary. Sources close to the team suggest Philadelphia would be open to a deal centred around young Wild center prospect Charlie Stramel, along with a future first-round pick, in exchange for sniper Owen Tippett. That arrangement would give Brière developmental assets while helping grease the wheels for Larkin's move to Minnesota. The Red Wings, meanwhile, would reportedly receive an impact NHL player among the pieces coming back for their captain. https://x.com/NHLRumourReport/status/2117293154995171530?s=20 It is worth noting that Montreal Canadiens GM Kent Hughes is also reportedly still in the mix. Hughes is said to be waiting for Larkin to add the Canadiens to his list of approved destinations. Recent reports also suggested that Detroit may have been interested in exploring teams such as Boston, Los Angeles, and Buffalo, but Larkin's camp has drawn a hard line. The Larkin file has dragged on for months now, and none of these reported frameworks have been confirmed by the teams involved. For now, all eyes are on whether the next few days finally bring the resolution that the hockey world has been anticipating.

item.description: The Texans made their final decision on David Montgomery for Week 9. We’re trying to get him on the field, trying to get him going,” Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters on November 4. “Right now, it’s still week to week, but he has made some progress.” Montgomery has been out since suffering his groing injury in the Texans’ Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans. Ryans said on Monday that they would monitor Montgomery throughout the week. However, there was also optimism about how Montgomery’s recovery process was trending before that. The Texans have missed Montgomery, whose absence from the practice field on Wednesday preceded Ryans’ official announcement. This will mark Montgomery’s third missed outing, one short of the minimum requirement for a player placed on injured reserve but designated to return. The Texans are also low on available designations, though, further complicating the situation. Alexander explained the fine line they are trying to walk. “The Texans have three returns remaining. With 10 games left, I don’t think it’s out of the question they could use it on Jordan at some point. The only other player eligible at the moment is running back British Brooks, whose primary role is special teams,” Alexander wrote on November 4 in response to a fan’s question. “I think the Texans wanted to leave their options open as opposed to not being able to use that spot on the practice squad.” The Texans certainly have decisions to make, including regarding Montgomery. item.title: Phillies Reportedly Looking To Add This Specific Type Of Pitcher This Offseason
item.description: Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Jhoan Duran The Philadelphia Phillies were eliminated in the National League Wild Card Series last season, and they may feel pressure to be aggressive in free agency as their championship window closes. Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber are not getting any younger, and it's hard to tell how much longer this roster can continue to play at a high level. The Phillies have some clear needs, and adding a reliable lefty in the bullpen is one of them. According to The Athletic's Matt Gelb , the Phillies will be in the market for a setup lefty in the bullpen. Jhoan Duran is about as good as it gets in the ninth inning, and the team has righties they trust to set him up. However, sometimes the lineup dictates the need for a southpaw in the eighth inning. If the Phillies want a lefty setup man, the perfect one is a free agent: Adrian Morejon. He received a qualifying offer from the San Diego Padres, but figures to land a multi-year deal somewhere. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! He was an All-Star in 2025 and was a huge part of what many considered the best bullpen in baseball this year. He posted a 2.83 ERA pitching in front of Mason Miller. In the last three years, he has posted a 2.58 ERA in 211 games. He has recorded 248 strikeouts in that span as well. The Phillies could really shorten games if they had him and Duran for the final six outs. If they want to know what that would look like, they can just look at how Miller and Morejon operated. Duran and Morejon would be just as good a duo. More MLB: Red Sox Reportedly Poach Yankees Triple-A Manager For Big League Staff

item.title: ‘Inexcusable and Semi-Reprehensible,’ ‘You’re Ruining Your Players’ — Bill Simmons Rips Adam Silver’s ‘Negligence and Greed’ Over 82-Game Schedule
item.description: ‘Inexcusable and Semi-Reprehensible,’ ‘You’re Ruining Your Players’ — Bill Simmons Rips Adam Silver’s ‘Negligence and Greed’ Over 82-Game Schedule Bill Simmons wants the NBA to cut its regular season from 82 games to 70, and he blames Commissioner Adam Silver and the league’s owners for the current schedule. The Ringer founder made his case on Tuesday’s episode of “The Bill Simmons Podcast.” His argument also centered on potential expansion in Las Vegas and Seattle, which could bring billions in fees to the league’s current owners. Bill Simmons Targets Adam Silver Over NBA Schedule and Potential Expansion Fees The podcaster opened his criticism by directing it at the league office. “Listen, I don’t know how many times I’ve talked about this on the pod about the schedule and about how this, to me, is just inexcusable and semi-reprehensible that whoever is in charge of the league, which I think is Adam Silver these days, that he doesn’t care,” Simmons said . The NBA has maintained an 82-game regular season since 1967-68, apart from seasons shortened by labor disputes or other disruptions. He continued, “You’re ruining your players … and you’re hurting careers, and you’re shortening careers. This should be a 70-game season. And if you talk to literally everybody who plays basketball, all of them would say the season needs to be shorter. And if you don’t do it at this point, I just think it’s negligent. I really do. I think it’s actual negligence and greed.” The NBA has 30 franchises, and adding teams in Las Vegas and Seattle would mark its first expansion since the Charlotte Bobcats joined the league in 2004. That potential expansion is central to Simmons’ argument because of the money he expects the league’s current owners to receive. “The question for me is, you’re gonna make all this money … that’s gonna be $9.5 billion for the [Las Vegas] expansion team … They’re gonna get a second thing from Seattle, which is gonna be $7.5 (billion), something like that. … So all these owners are getting, I don’t know, $16 billion in expansion fees,” he said. Those figures are his estimates. In March, the New York Post reported that expansion fees could range from $7 billion to $10 billion per team, with the money going to the NBA’s current owners rather than being shared with players. Cutting 12 games from each team’s schedule would also mean fewer home dates and fewer opportunities to sell tickets and concessions. item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United’s unlikely one-match winning streak and hard-to-please fans
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Considering they’d just gone nine games without a win, assorted Manchester United fans carping about the manner of their team’s Bigger Cup win over Roma on shouty radio phone-ins on Tuesday night struck Football Daily as the type who’d complain about a firefighter refusing to wipe their boots at the front door before rescuing them from a burning house. Yes, it’s true that United played appallingly in the first half and were lucky to be only 2-0 down. And yes, the penalty was somewhat fortuitous against a knack-ravaged Serie A side who have form in coughing up two-goal leads in the competition. However, when your once mighty side has spent the opening months of the season looking more like a broken washing machine full of spanners falling down an escalator than an elite football team, complaining about the artistic merit of a highly unlikely comeback win seems unnecessarily churlish, even if Matheus Cunha’s celebration of the winner was a little over the top. Roma managed to capitulate to Manchester United while being 2-0 up. Even Man Utd haven’t managed to do that too many times but I wouldn’t describe their second half performance as ‘ a comeback for the ages ’. Their opponents just didn’t turn up” – Nigel Sanders. These suggestions of paper and velcro shirts seem overly complicated. ( yesterday’s Football Daily letters ). If teams would just commit to using body paint instead of clothing, the foul becomes impossible to commit unless a defender is possessed of both long fingernails and a cavalier disregard for the health of their opponent. Also, no more tedious yellow cards for removing the shirt after a goal. Win win” – Ben Mimmack. Poor Nuno can take comfort that he’s in a long list of managers seen off by a poor result against West Brom since 2010, including Chris Hughton twice and five others. If you add Roberto di Matteo (he clung on for one more game) and spoiling Alex Ferguson’s leaving do with a 5-5 draw we were responsible for nine dismissals in seven years between 2010 and 2017. I think that’s pretty impressive. We’ve been quiet since then but perhaps we’re going for another run – championship managers beware” – Tom Levesley. item.description: Mauricio Pochettino names 25-man roster to face Haiti McKennie and Sullivan among notable inclusions Quarter-final matches set for Miami, Cincinnati Mauricio Pochettino has selected his 25-man roster for the United States’ Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti, including recalls for Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun. After 13 players earned their first caps in the previous window, only two selections could be in line for international debuts this month. The two-leg series against Haiti marks the first competitive action for the US since they exited the World Cup with a calamitous showing against Belgium in the last 16. Pochettino’s side are heavily favored to win the Nations League outright, arriving in better form and health than chief rivals Mexico and Canada. Haiti will host their “home” leg in Miami on 14 November due to years-long security issues stemming from widespread gang violence in Port-au-Prince. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him. item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
item.description: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final . On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or , the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious. It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good. Continue reading...

item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
